709870.t: Traditionally derived from ὄψ (óps, “eye”) + θάλαμος (thálamos, “chamber”), but note the usual ancient Greek word for eye is the similar ὤψ (ṓps), with a long /o/.

709844.t: Of disputed origin, with multiple theories proposed: * Perhaps from an older *(ϝ)ορσανός (*(w)orsanós), which may be related to οὐρέω (ouréō, “to urinate”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₁worseye-, from *h₁wers- (“rain”) (compare Sanskrit वर्षति (varṣati, “it…

709852.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂ṓws (“ear”), the oblique stem being from a lengthened form *h₂ows-n̥t- (for which compare Old Armenian ունկն (unkn)).

709884.t: Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *woǵʰlos, from Proto-Indo-European *weǵʰ- (“to drive, transport”) (whence also ὄχος (ókhos) and Arcadocypriot Greek ϝέχω (wékhō, “to bear, bring”)), with cognates such as Old Norse vagl.

709879.t: From Proto-Hellenic *opʰrū́s, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃bʰrúHs (“eyebrow”). Cognates include Sanskrit भ्रू (bhrū́), Lithuanian bruvis, Tocharian B pärwāne, Old English brū (English brow).

709835.t: According to Beekes (2010), “the relation between οὖν and ὦν is unclear. Unconvincing explanations in Brugmann-Thumb 1913: 633 and in Schwyzer 1950: 586f.

709803.t: Originally the neuter accusative singular of ὅστις (hóstĭs, “whoever; whichever; whatever”, indefinite relative pronoun), lexicalised as a conjunction.

709858.t: Synchronically analyzable as ὁ (ho, “self; third-person pronoun”) + αὐτός (autós, “self; third-person pronoun”).

709875.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ókʷʰis, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ógʷʰis (“snake”). Cognates include Sanskrit अहि॑ (áhi), Avestan 𐬀𐬲𐬌 (aži), Old Armenian իժ (iž), and English ask (“eft; newt; lizard”).

709839.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *h₁ers- (“tail, butt”) (alternatively reconstructed as Proto-Indo-European *h₃érsos (“backside, buttocks”)), and related to ὄρρος (órrhos, “butt, ass”); see there for more.

709817.t: From οὐδέ (oudé, “and not, not even”) + εἷς (heîs, “one”). Sometimes reanalysed as οὐ (ou, “no, not”) + δείς (deís, “no one, nothing”), as a result of the later variant, οὐθείς (outheís).

709805.t: Possibly οὐκί (oukí, “not so, never”), from Proto-Hellenic *oyuki, from Proto-Indo-European *(ne) h₂óyu kʷíd (“(not) ever, (not) on your life”). Compare Sanskrit उद् (ud), Old Armenian ոչ (očʻ), and Albanian as.

709867.t: From Proto-Hellenic *opʰelos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃bʰel- (“to increase, augment”) (whence also ὀφείλω (opheílō, “to owe, be obligated”)). Cognates include Old Armenian աւելի (aweli, “more”), յաւելում (yawelum, “I add”).

709865.t: From Proto-Hellenic *opʰél͏̌l͏̌ō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃bʰélyeti, from *h₃bʰel- (whence ὄφελος (óphelos, “benefit”)).

709806.t: PIE word *swé From Proto-Hellenic *hwe (= *ϝ̔έ (*whé), representing the accusative case), from Proto-Indo-European *swé (reflexive pronoun).

709851.t: From οὐρέω (ouréō, “to urinate”). Not related to Latin ūrīna.

d: οὕτω ποτ’ ἦν μῦς καὶ γαλῆ

709801.t: Univerbation of ὅτ’ (hót’, “when”) + ἄν (ắn, modal particle).

709802.t: From ὅς (hós) + τε (te). Compare τότε (tóte), πότε (póte), ποτέ (poté).

709807.t: Traditionally compared with the set Latin vae, Gothic 𐍅𐌰𐌹 (wai), etc., from Proto-Indo-European *wáy, but it is not derivable from there through regular sound laws.

709855.t: From οὖσα (oûsă, feminine present participle of εἰμί (eimĭ́, “to be”)) + -ία (-ĭ́ā, abstract noun suffix). Literally, “beingness”.

709896.t: From a derivative of Proto-Indo-European *h₁epi (“on”); related to ὀπίσω (opísō, “after”) and ὄπισθεν (ópisthen, “in the future”).

709834.t: From an archaic form *ϝουλή (*woulḗ), from Proto-Indo-European *welh₃- (“to hit”). Closest cognates are Latin vulnus (“wound”) and Irish fuil (“blood”).

709845.t: From Proto-Hellenic *eworhéyō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁wors-éye-ti (“to make it rain”), from *h₁wers-.

709883.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂ogʰléyeti, from *h₂egʰ- (“to be upset, afraid”). By surface analysis, ὄχλος (ókhlos) + -έω (-éō).
